The project: plain files, one folder per tool
gui.json, graph-flow.json, graph-nodes.json, graph-schedule.json: the GUI, the wires, the nodes' settings, the schedule
nodes/<id>/ input.js, output.js, code.js or prompt.md, history.md: what a node is and how it was written
state.json (and states/): what using it left behind. Beside the project, never in it. examples/, notebook-examples/: projects that tests and CI run
Where it happens: pressing Send in a delivered tool
A person presses Send, or a block fires
GuiApp.tsx and the block's WidgetView call start.ts: startRound(event, values)
kit/api/port.ts: POST /api/runtime/rounds, answered at once with a round id (the answer comes on the stream)
host/serve.ts finds the handler of the route in host/api.ts, refuses what the tool does not offer
host/session.ts holds the graph in use; host/rounds.ts runs one round at a time
The engine orders and runs it
runtime/localCore.ts, behind protocol.ts, hands it to executor.ts, which orders the nodes (graph/order.ts, triggers.ts)
nodes/<kind>/<Kind>NodeRunner.ts: a code node in nodes/body.ts, an ai node through ai/providers.ts (settings.ts says which model)
latch.ts keeps each node's last output; session.ts keeps what a person or memory node keeps in state.json
the stream: kit/api/session.ts feeds the store, GuiApp.tsx and the WidgetViews redraw
Where it happens: ✨ Generate in the editor
A person presses ✨ on a node file
node/usePartGenerate.ts, from NodeView.tsx or a chat (PartChat.tsx)
writing/useGenerate.ts keeps the state; api/client.ts: POST /api/ai/generate
backend/editor/host/routes.ts calls the writer, with the request's progress id
The prompt is made, the model asked
editor/graph/generate.ts builds it (graph/editor/prompts.ts and the node's files), through the one model client
The answer is read and written
backend/authoring/ask.ts reads the fenced block and keeps the transcript; the file is written into nodes/<id>/ and history.md
